A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Rewarding Doubt. Their text, figures, tables, equations and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite restructuring.

before.justification: v3 reports original LLM fine-tuning and evaluation results, including calibration, accuracy and transfer experiments on TriviaQA, QAMPARI, CommonsenseQA and MedQA.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds evaluated RL baselines and comparisons across additional language models in Tables 1 and 3.

M1.justification: The two-stage answer/confidence generation, confidence-only optimization, logarithmic reward and LoRA fine-tuning are retained. Naming PPO and specifying the clipping constant add implementation information without establishing a changed procedure. Both clipped and unclipped reward expressions already appear in v3.

E1.justification: Both versions use TriviaQA, QAMPARI, CommonsenseQA and MedQA, retaining single-answer, multiple-answer and multiple-choice tasks and their transfer scenarios. Additional language-model configurations do not introduce new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v4 Table 1 adds PPO-M and PPO-C while retaining the existing comparators. These substantially extend the primary comparison to directly relevant RL confidence-training methods. SteerConf is added to related work but is not evaluated.

E3.justification: Beyond v3's Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct experiments, v4 Table 3 adds LLaMA-3.1-8B, Qwen-2.5-3B, Qwen-2.5-7B and Gemma-2-9B configurations. This substantially expands architecture and size settings. Existing prompts, stated training budgets, correctness thresholds and evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 adds an explicit cross-model consistency study testing whether calibration improvements persist across architectures and parameter scales, with evidence in Table 3. This introduces a substantial robustness question beyond v3's single-model evaluation. Existing cross-dataset and single-to-multiple-answer transfer analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v3 reports point estimates; v4 adds 95% confidence intervals throughout Tables 1–5 and standard errors for the externally sourced LACIE results. No interval-estimation procedure, seeds or repeated-run counts are documented, so this establishes expanded uncertainty reporting without establishing additional training runs.

E6.justification: New results include PPO-M/PPO-C ECE values of 0.3262/0.3607 and four model-comparison blocks. For example, v4 Table 3 reports Qwen-2.5-3B ECE of 0.5330 for Verbalize versus 0.1483 for Rewarding Doubt. Existing Rewarding Doubt benchmark and transfer point estimates are retained; several baseline accuracy entries receive 0.0001 updates. The earlier qualitative observation of fixed-confidence collapse is removed.

T1.justification: The calibration definition, MDP, Proposition 1 and Appendix B proof are unchanged. v4 foregrounds the unclipped logarithmic score already given in v3 Appendix B, while new Appendix C repeats the existing clipped formula. No new theorem or corrected derivation is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: directly training confidence expression with a proper-scoring-rule reward, claimed optimal calibration, improved empirical calibration and transfer without further fine-tuning. Additional experiments support these retained claims.

C2.justification: The main interpretation remains stable, but v4 removes the observed fixed-confidence convergence limitation and proposed stabilizing remedies, and adds the explicit 3B–9B scale boundary. Binary correctness remains the current applicability boundary, with proposed extensions to LLM judges and preference rewards. The transfer comparison is narrowed from outperforming baseline methods to outperforming the base model.

D1.justification: v4 first specifies PPO and epsilon = 0.001, and replaces a promised public code release with a stated public repository link. Conversely, v3's exact parameter counts and Asset Details appendix containing dataset/model access links and licenses disappear. Baseline implementation details are relocated to Appendix D rather than removed.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands research positioning around supervised confidence expression and its dependence on constructed confidence targets. It adds numerous relevant works, including SteerConf, Leng et al.'s reward calibration, R-tuning and other supervised approaches, while dropping the Quark reference. The distinction from prior training approaches is developed more fully.

P1.justification: Related work is extensively rewritten into three subsections. Training implementation is folded into Experimental Setup, baseline details move to the appendix, and reproducibility and LLM-use statements are added. Reward explanations and limitations are revised, with additional changes to author order, contribution notes and citation style.

P2.justification: v4 adds the model-comparison table, merges the earlier CommonsenseQA and MedQA tables, and reformats all main result tables to accommodate uncertainty intervals. Figures and tables are repositioned, and title, headers and typography change throughout. Figure 3 rescales confidence from 0–1 to 0–10 while preserving the equivalent reward plot.

improvement.justification: The additional model study and relevant RL baselines strengthen empirical support beyond v3's single-model evaluation, while expanded related work and explicit PPO/clipping details improve assessability. These gains are tempered by undocumented confidence-interval procedures and sparse details for new comparisons. Removing v3's observed fixed-confidence-collapse limitation without evidence of resolution also weakens transparency. The net improvement is therefore limited.
